title: Normalized exact integer-orbit induction for additive autoequivalences
statement: Let $A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category in its morphism universe [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], and let $F:A\to A$ be an additive equivalence functor. There is a functor $I:A\to A^F$, left adjoint to the fixed-pair forgetful functor [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Its carrier is the coproduct of $(F.asEquivalence)^n(X)$ over all integers. There are natural successor comparisons $(F.asEquivalence)^n\circ F\simeq(F.asEquivalence)^{n+1}$ such that the structure map sends the translated nth coprojection to the $(n+1)$st coprojection. The adjunction bijection restricts a map to its zeroth coprojection. On actual carrier maps $I$ preserves addition. It preserves all finite limits and finite colimits.

proof.text: Reuse Free.functor F and Free.adjunction F from WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Endofunctor.IsoAlgebra, whose objects are the explicit integer coproducts. Identify their recursive positive and negative iterates with functor iterates by induction. Equivalence.powNat agrees with those iterates by two-step induction. The resulting natural successor comparison is obtained from Free.objSucc by these equalities; its naturality is Free.map_objMap_comp_objSucc. Transport Free.map_ι_comp_str through Sigma.mapIso to obtain the stated shift formula. Free.adjunction is definitionally restriction to the zero summand, and Sigma.ι_mapIso_hom verifies its normalization.

Prove additivity using Free.hom_ext at the zero summand and Sigma.ι_map. The Grothendieck AB4 instance gives stability of monomorphisms under integer coproducts (Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Abelian.GrothendieckAxioms.Colim). Hence Free.functor preserves monomorphisms by the source Free instance. Its adjunction supplies preservation of cokernels and finite colimits. Apply Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesMonos_and_cokernels and Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesHomology from Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.ShortComplex.ExactFunctor to obtain finite limits. These facts also cover zero objects and the zero category.
